basis: WOOF forecast throughput measured on dated end-to-end runs: cell-steps per second, default suite (Morrison or Thompson microphysics, YSU, Noah, RTE+RRTMGP), 49 levels. A cell-step is one grid cell advanced one model step.

full_product_stack.note: Thompson, MYNN, RUC, legacy RRTMG at 59 levels on the reference card. The gap to the default suite is split by measured share: MYNN 0.48, legacy RRTMG 0.19, RUC 0.16, the rest 0.17 when all three run together.

bandwidth_only.note: Cards with no WOOF measurement. They take the factor of the measured card nearest in memory bandwidth, and the estimate says confidence low.

per_step_floor_s.note: Small grids are launch bound: a 100 x 80 x 49 grid at 3 km ran 720 steps in 16.9 s on an RTX 4090, far above what its cell count alone predicts. The floor scales with the square root of the card factor.

fixed_costs.fetch_note: 8 HRRR full files (4.2 GB) in 130 s, about 37 MB/s, from the public mirror.
fixed_costs.prepare_note: 38.8 s for a 100 x 80 HRRR grid over 4 forcing times; scaled by (grid columns x forcing times) to the power 0.6, an assumption until this machine has its own runs.
fixed_costs.compile_note: First run of a physics suite compiles its kernels (about 50 s); zero once warm or after woof warm-kernels.
fixed_costs.render_note: Pictures are drawn while the forecast runs; only the last frame is drawn after it.

global.reference: T255, 24 h, RTX 4090: 439 s whole run, 234 s integration, 10.7 GiB card; statics 874 s once per truncation on CPU

hex.reference: x1.40962 mesh (40,962 cells), 1 h forecast in 241 s on an RTX PRO 4500 with 3.2 GB host memory
